elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 8.2 now reads "neither Array nor its Controlled Affiliates shall Commercialize in the Ono Territory" — Ono and its Affiliates are removed from the covenant. The post-termination tail ("neither Ono nor its Affiliates shall Commercialize a Competing Product ... prior to the [ * ] anniversary") and Array's enforcement right ("If Ono Commercializes a Competing Product ... Array may immediately terminate this Agreement") are deleted. Article IX supply terms are requirements-supply by Array with Ono expressly retaining the right to Manufacture or engage a Subcontractor, which is not a Customer-side sole-supplier promise; the Section 2.1 licences run in Customer's favour. Deterministic check "no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains" is ok.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the redline no exclusivity covenant binds Ono at all, so there is no Customer-side restriction requiring category limitation. The only surviving restriction (on Array/its Controlled Affiliates) benefits Customer and is outside this checklist.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the open-ended "Prior to the [ * ]" restraint and the post-termination "[ * ] anniversary" tail on Ono are both struck, leaving no Customer exclusivity period to cap.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no Customer exclusivity obligation remaining, no performance-based exit is required. (The retained sentence terminating the royalty payment period if Array Commercializes a Competing Product operates in Customer's favour.)

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no Customer-side exclusivity survives the redline, so no automatic lapse on Array supply/delivery failure is needed.

elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Restated for completeness: the preferred outcome is achieved, which necessarily satisfies the weaker fallback constraint set.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the operative text of Section 8.2 binds only Array and its Controlled Affiliates; every Ono-side restraint (in-term covenant, post-termination [ * ]-anniversary tail) and the Array termination right that enforced it are removed.

Edits are confined to what removing the Customer-side covenant requires. Array's reciprocal restriction and the Customer-favourable royalty-termination sentence ("If during the [ * ], Array Commercializes a Competing Product ... Ono may continue to Commercialize the Product") are retained verbatim, as are the definitional sentences and the avoidance-of-doubt carve-out.

Deleting "If Ono Commercializes a Competing Product ... Array may immediately terminate this Agreement" is necessary rather than extra: it is the enforcement mechanic for the struck covenant and would otherwise be a contingent right with no underlying obligation.

Conforming Section 14.2(a)(i) from "pursuant to Section 8.2, 13.3 or 13.4" to "pursuant to Section 13.3 or 13.4" is the minimum edit needed to avoid a dangling cross-reference to a now-nonexistent Section 8.2 termination; the cost-allocation mechanics for Sections 13.2/13.3/13.4 and the wind-down cost split survive unchanged.

Intent preserved: supply mechanics in Article IX, the Section 2.1 inbound licences, royalty-term mechanics and termination rights under Sections 13.2/13.3/13.4 are untouched, and no retained sentence contradicts the narrowed Section 8.2. No undefined term is created ("Competing Product" is still defined in the retained Array-side sentence).

Drafting caution (not a defect found here): confirm no other provision outside the cited paragraphs cross-references a termination "pursuant to Section 8.2" or otherwise assumes an Ono non-compete; if one exists it must be conformed the same way.
